newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Private label growth too fast-David Jones.
newsitem.headline: Private label growth too fast-David Jones.

text.p: Upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd said on Monday that while private label apparel remained an important part of its brand mix, its share of that mix had grown too quickly.

"In that mix, there will be a place for the private label programme that we currently have in place, but I do think that we have probably over-extended that," chief executive officer Peter Wilkinson told an Australian Fashion Week seminar in his first public appearance since taking the top job.

"When I looked at the numbers, I noted with some interest that we increased our private label programme from around 13 percent to 26 percent of volume in apparel and that seems to me too quick, a little too much."
Signalling a shift in product focus, Wilkinson said the private label would be repositioned so as not to cannibalise other components of the brand mix.

"I have little doubt that as we move to reposition that brand to play a role in our mix, it will be more mainstream, it will be conservative," Wilkinson said, stressing complementarity with other labels sold by the upmarket department store.
"It will add value to other brands in the business, it will not consume of replace them."

Wilkinson replaced former CEO Chris Tideman in mid-March and was previously managing director of jeans retailer Just Jeans Holdings Ltd. Prior to that he was managing director of Coles Myer Ltd's Myer Grace department store chain.
On March 12, the company announced a 50 percent fall in first half net profit to A$22.34 and said the year net profit would be lower than the previous year.
The company had previously warned of a fall in first half profit due to a lacklustre retail environment.
By 3.15 p.m. (0315 GMT), David Jones shares were a cent lower at A$1.66 on turnover of 320,415 shares.
